rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the setumah the row cites for its opening sits AFTER MT 57:14, so it corroborates a cut at MT 57:14|57:15 — exactly where the span's only koh-amar frame stands — while the row's actual front-seam frame form is never quoted and the rival opening is never disclosed; plus a frame-class grouping imprecision. LF: device_notes describes the distant-verse comparison using the writer's own batch language rather than by content.
rulings.grounds: DISTINCT defects. OL's core is UPHELD on bytes and on the extractor's own keying. The parashah layer is built by walking the source and attaching each seg to the verse element it falls inside, so a seg keyed at a verse marks the break AFTER that verse's words. The inventory puts a SAMEKH at MT 57:14 and a SAMEKH at MT 57:21: the first therefore corroborates a break at MT 57:14 | MT 57:15 — span-INTERNAL to this row — while the row's actual front seam, MT 57:13 | MT 57:14, carries no mark of any layer. The convention is corroborated inside this very stretch: the other three setumot here (MT 57:21, MT 58:14, MT 59:21) each sit on a verse that its own unit reads as a CLOSE, which only break-after keying explains. And two independent signals converge on MT 57:15 as a rival opening: that seg, and the span's only divine frame — כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֗א שֹׁכֵ֥ן עַד֙ וְקָד֣וֹשׁ (oshb:Isa.57.15, byte tier), whose formula head is כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר and whose speaker is named by epithet with no tetragrammaton anywhere in the verse. The row discloses neither; its rejected alternative addresses only the closing pair at web:Isa.57.20. UPHELD. Second OL item UPHELD: the row's own front-seam driver is the speech-introduction form וְאָמַ֥ר standing verse-initial at oshb:Isa.57.14 (byte tier) — byte-present but never quoted, the seam argued entirely from the English rendering. Third, OL's credits verify exactly: a paseq seg and a ketiv/qere note both stand at MT 57:19; the K/Q pair is the unpointed ketiv running straight into the pointed qere, נוב נִ֣יב, and the row's quoted run שָׁל֨וֹם שָׁל֜וֹם לָרָח֧וֹק וְלַקָּר֛וֹב אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה (byte tier) does begin after that pair; and the distant comparison is byte-exact — אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י לָרְשָׁעִֽים (oshb:Isa.57.21) against אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים (oshb:Isa.48.22), both byte tier, identical in four of five tokens and differing only in the divine-name token (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the shared verb-pair run at byte tier). The row states that difference correctly and calls it a divine-name substitution rather than a repeated refrain — exemplary handling, not a defect. REFUTED, with the bytes: OL's fourth item. It charges that the shared property holds for only one of the three cited parallels because MT 42:5 and MT 51:22 do carry the tetragrammaton. But the property the row actually states is the NON-ADJACENT divine-frame form — a koh-amar frame whose divine designation is a title rather than the bare adjacent tetragrammaton — and all three cited members carry it: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.30.12), כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5) and כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנַ֣יִךְ יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.51.22), each byte tier, each interposing a title before or in place of the tetragrammaton. OL substituted a different property for the row's own. The omission of כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י לֵ֚ךְ (oshb:Isa.21.6, byte tier, the intervening-dative member) is likewise not a defect: the row writes 'also carried at', claims no exhaustive set, and so owes no digit. LF's item is UPHELD at low: device_notes calls the distant comparison 'cross-part texture', naming the writer's own batch structure rather than the two verses' relationship in Isaiah's text — barred in every field. This is the SAME register class carried by three more rows in this cluster and by the row closing at web:Isa.55.13, so it is a part-wide sweep, not a spot fix.
rulings.remedy: Author work order. (a) boundary_evidence_refs + device_notes: stop citing the MT 57:14 seg as opening evidence. State in PROSE that the break it corroborates falls after MT 57:14, i.e. span-internal at MT 57:14 | MT 57:15, and that the row's own front seam carries no mark of any layer (absence is never counterevidence). TEST (the check that killed the original): for every parashah citation in the row, the verse key must equal the verse the break follows, and each edge claim must name which seam it corroborates. (b) strongest_rejected_alternative: disclose the MT 57:15 rival opening and name BOTH converging signals — the seg after MT 57:14 and the span's only divine frame — while keeping the tier-3 signal explicitly non-driving. (c) boundary_rationale: splice the verse-initial speech-introduction form at oshb:Isa.57.14 so the front seam rests on Hebrew, not on the English. TEST: the front-seam sentence must survive deletion of its WEB quote. (d) device_notes: replace 'cross-part texture' with a content-only description of the two verses' relationship; run the same purge across the whole part. TEST: no field may contain a phrase naming a part, batch, assigned range or row order. (e) NO CHANGE required to the frame-class sentence or to the distant-comparison byte analysis — both are correct as written; adding the intervening-dative member is optional enrichment, not a cure.

rulings.challenge_claim: device_notes twice identifies neighboring material by its position in the writer's row/part sequence rather than by verse content alone — 'this part's own opening row' and the mark disclosure given 'at the prior row's close'.
rulings.grounds: Both phrases are present verbatim in device_notes, and both name the writer's own batching rather than the verses' place in Isaiah's text: the sabbath echo is attributed to 'this part's own opening row' instead of to web:Isa.56.2 / web:Isa.56.4 / web:Isa.56.6 by verse, and the front-seam mark is said to have been 'disclosed already at the prior row's close' instead of being stated on its own. The register purge bars positional row references and file-order talk in every field, and cross-row references must be verse-anchored. UPHELD at LF's medium: two breaches in one field, in a row that otherwise handles its layers well. The underlying argument verifies and deserves the credit LF gives it: קְרָ֤א בְגָרוֹן֙ אַל תַּחְשֹׂ֔ךְ reaches byte tier verse-initially at oshb:Isa.58.1, and the closing signature כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר reaches byte tier at oshb:Isa.58.14 and stands in exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, MT 1:20, MT 40:5, MT 58:14), so treating it as a formal close is byte-warranted. The mark handling is exactly right on both edges under break-after keying: the SAMEKH keyed at MT 57:21 marks the break after MT 57:21 — precisely this row's front seam — and the SAMEKH keyed at MT 58:14 marks the break after its closing verse; no paseq, ketiv/qere or special-letter object falls anywhere in MT 58:1-58:14, so the disclosure set is complete with nothing owed. That correct edge usage is worth recording beside the mis-attribution found on the preceding row: the same writer read the layer correctly here. NEW FINDING neither primary made: the row's strongest_rejected_alternative names the 'then' pivot at web:Isa.58.8, but the byte-hardest internal candidate lies earlier. The address is masculine SINGULAR at MT 58:1, masculine PLURAL through MT 58:3-58:6 — לְהַשְׁמִ֥יעַ closing MT 58:4 and חָפְשִׁ֔ים closing MT 58:6, both byte tier — and masculine SINGULAR again from MT 58:7, הֲל֨וֹא פָרֹ֤ס לָֽרָעֵב֙ לַחְמֶ֔ךָ (byte tier). So the grammatical turn sits at MT 58:6 | MT 58:7, and the disclosed rival does not touch it. The row's continuity claim still survives, because its anchors at MT 58:8 and MT 58:13 are both continuous with MT 58:7 — but a stronger rival than the one disclosed exists in the bytes.
rulings.remedy: Author work order. (a) device_notes: re-state the sabbath echo by verse alone (web:Isa.56.2, web:Isa.56.4, web:Isa.56.6) with no reference to any row, part or batch, and state the front-seam mark disclosure on its own terms rather than by deferral to another row's close. TEST: no field may contain a phrase naming a part, batch, assigned range or row order, and every cross-row reference must be verse-anchored — sweep the whole part, since this class recurs on three further rows here. (b) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace or supplement the web:Isa.58.8 pivot with the byte-harder candidate at the MT 58:6 | MT 58:7 address turn, spliced and stated as a grammatical number change, and say why the unit still holds (the continuity anchors at MT 58:8 and MT 58:13 are continuous with MT 58:7). TEST: a second-person form census over MT 58:1-58:14 must reproduce the replacement sentence with both witnesses' English removed. NOT author work: any actual respan at MT 58:6 | MT 58:7 is a boundary proposal for the boss.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: device_notes twice identifies neighboring rows by their position in the writer's sequence rather than by verse content alone. OL: the opening driver is a presentative particle that stands twice inside the immediately preceding span; a two-site book-wide phrase on the row's own closing verse and a chapter-length salvation-root inclusio are undisclosed; and the signal-class field is empty.
rulings.grounds: DISTINCT defects; both real, one of OL's mis-objected. LF's item is UPHELD at medium and verified verbatim: device_notes says the front-seam mark was 'disclosed already at the prior row's close' and that the closing argument 'rests on the person shift that opens the next row at Isa.59.9, disclosed there as that row's own frame signal'. Both name row order in the writer's sequence; the second also outsources this row's own closing warrant to another row, which verse-anchored cross-referencing exists to prevent. OL's particle item is UPHELD with its TIER supplied: הֵ֛ן לֹֽא קָצְרָ֥ה יַד יְהוָ֖ה מֵֽהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ reaches byte tier at oshb:Isa.59.1, but the same presentative stands mid-verse at MT 58:3 (וְלֹ֣א) and verse-initially at MT 58:4 (הֵ֣ן), both inside the preceding unit, and it carries no frame role at any of the three sites. OL cites all three as byte tier — true of each splice against its own verse, but the RECURRENCE is not byte: the MT 59:1 form הֵ֛ן stands at byte tier in only 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, MT 55:4 and MT 59:1) and meets the MT 58:3 / MT 58:4 forms at accent-stripped tier. The finding stands on the corrected tier: the row's boundary rests on the person turn and the tier-3 mark, not on the particle its rationale leads with. OL's phrase item is REFINED — right digit, wrong count-object. The run OL quotes, וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָ֑ם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier), stands in exactly ONE verse book-wide at skeleton tier, not two; so does the two-token prefixed run וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט. The 2-verse digit belongs to the UNPREFIXED core: that object stands in exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT 59:8 and MT 59:15), its partner being אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט at oshb:Isa.59.15. A reproduced digit carrying the wrong count-object is itself the defect class the campaign names; the underlying finding — a two-site pairing on this row's own closing verse whose partner sits past the seam — survives on the corrected object. OL's inclusio item is UPHELD and verified: the salvation root inside the row's own opening splice, מֵֽהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ, returns at וַתּ֤וֹשַֽׁע (oshb:Isa.59.16) and וְכ֥וֹבַע יְשׁוּעָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.59.17), all byte tier — the salvation family, correctly kept apart from the prophet's name, which shares consonants but not this order. OL's last item is the row's most machine-checkable defect and is UNDERWEIGHTED at low: observed_substrate_signals is EMPTY. The field contract is ratified day-one — every row's oss carries dotted signal keys naming the signal classes consulted — and this row's own drivers (an assertion onset and an addressee turn) both have classes available. An empty oss on a row that argues two signals in prose is a straight contract breach, and oss is the dependent field every driver repair must re-derive. Combined severity therefore sits at medium, not low. Verified true: the masculine-plural address does run MT 59:2-59:3 and turns to third-person description at MT 59:4, the row's disclosed rival is a live one, and the mark claim is byte-correct — the SAMEKH keyed at MT 58:14 marks the break after that verse, i.e. this row's front seam, and no mark, paseq or ketiv/qere object falls anywhere inside MT 59:1-59:8.
rulings.remedy: Author work order. (a) observed_substrate_signals: populate it with dotted signal keys for the row's actual drivers — the assertion onset and the addressee/person turn — and mirror them in the prose. TEST: the field is non-empty, every entry is a dotted taxonomy key, and no staged-file name or stem appears. (b) device_notes: re-state the front-seam mark disclosure on its own terms and re-anchor the closing argument to verses rather than to another row's position; the closing warrant must stand in this row's own prose. TEST: no field names a part, batch, assigned range or row order; sweep the whole part. (c) boundary_rationale: demote the presentative particle from lead warrant — disclose that it stands twice in the immediately preceding unit and name the accent-stripped tier of that recurrence — and lead instead with the person turn. TEST: collate the three spliced particle forms against each other and record the returned tier, which must not be reported as byte. (d) device_notes: disclose the two-site pairing on the CORRECT object — the unprefixed no-justice core at oshb:Isa.59.8 with its partner at oshb:Isa.59.15 (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier) — never the three-token run, which has no partner; and disclose the salvation-root inclusio running from the opening splice through oshb:Isa.59.16 and oshb:Isa.59.17. TEST (the check that killed the original): each quoted run must be swept in the exact form quoted, and its digit must match that form's own hit count.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's sole boundary driver is a form-class claim about MT 59:10-59:12 asserted from English renderings with no pointed splice, and the two-site book-wide phrase that brackets the span at both its seams is undisclosed in either direction.
rulings.grounds: OL's framing is exactly right: the underlying facts check out, so the defect is ENGAGEMENT, not truth. Verified at byte tier: MT 59:9-59:14 contains no vav-consecutive imperfect — נְגַֽשְׁשָׁ֤ה כַֽעִוְרִים֙ קִ֔יר and כָּשַׁ֤לְנוּ at oshb:Isa.59.10, כִּֽי רַבּ֤וּ פְשָׁעֵ֨ינוּ֙ and וַעֲוֺנֹתֵ֖ינוּ יְדַֽעֲנֽוּם at oshb:Isa.59.12, and וְהֻסַּ֤ג אָחוֹר֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט at oshb:Isa.59.14 (a vav plus perfect, not a wayyiqtol) — while oshb:Isa.59.15 opens וַתְּהִ֤י הָֽאֱמֶת֙ נֶעְדֶּ֔רֶת and continues וַיַּ֧רְא יְהוָ֛ה וַיֵּ֥רַע בְּעֵינָ֖יו (byte tier). But the row splices Hebrew for its opening verse only; every enumerated form at MT 59:10, MT 59:11 and MT 59:12 is carried on a translation, and no morphology layer is staged, so the row's own load-bearing claim cannot be checked from the row itself. UPHELD. NEW FINDING neither primary made, and it sharpens the charge: even the ONE Hebrew run the row does splice fails to display the form-class its driver names. The opening splice is עַל כֵּ֗ן רָחַ֤ק מִשְׁפָּט֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ (oshb:Isa.59.9, byte tier) — a third-person verb with a first-person-plural suffix on the preposition, not a first-person-plural verb; the verse's first actual first-person-plural verbs, נְקַוֶּ֤ה and נְהַלֵּֽךְ (byte tier), both fall OUTSIDE the quoted run. So the row's claim to argue the voice shift 'from the verb bytes themselves' is not demonstrated by its own quoted bytes at any point in the row. Bracket item UPHELD with the object tightened: OL pairs a waw-prefixed run at MT 59:8 with a ki-prefixed run at MT 59:15 and calls it 'the same phrase ... in exactly 2 verses'; the shared object is the unprefixed core, which stands in exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT 59:8 and MT 59:15) — the verse immediately before this row's front seam and the verse immediately after its back seam, a bracket around the whole span disclosed at neither. OL's catchword digits are EXACT and re-derived: the justice noun stands in 40 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, 5 of them in MT ch 59 (MT 59:8, 59:9, 59:11, 59:14, 59:15). Verified true: no petuchah, setumah, paseq or ketiv/qere object falls at MT 59:8 | MT 59:9 or anywhere inside MT 59:9-59:14, exactly as the row claims. Noted for the ledger: the other primary SUPPORTED this row and credited its verb-form check as byte-verified; that credit is over-extended, since the row's own splice does not carry the form class.
rulings.remedy: Author work order. (a) boundary_rationale: splice the pointed forms the driver enumerates — at least one first-person-plural verb from oshb:Isa.59.10 and one from oshb:Isa.59.12 — and re-cut the opening splice so it reaches a first-person-plural verb rather than stopping at the prepositional suffix. TEST (the check that killed the original): the voice-shift sentence must survive deletion of every WEB rendering in the row, and each form class named must be visible in a quoted pointed run. (b) boundary_rationale: state the form-class claim as a byte-checkable claim argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, since no morphology layer is staged — the same discipline digits get. (c) device_notes: disclose the bracket on the CORRECT object — the unprefixed no-justice core standing on the verse before the front seam and the verse after the back seam (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier) — and the density of the justice catchword in the chapter (sweep: 40 verses book-wide, 5 in MT ch 59), stating that neither moves the seams. TEST: each quoted run swept in the exact form quoted, its digit matching that form's own hit count.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: boundary_rationale identifies the row's own closing verse by its position in the writer's assigned batch rather than by its place in Isaiah's text. OL: the two distinct frame forms carrying the row's seam judgements at MT 59:20 and MT 59:21 are asserted from English only, the narrative chain byte-terminates one verse before the prose carries it, and the catchwords crossing the closing seam are undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: DISTINCT defects; both real, and LF's is UNDERWEIGHTED at low — I raise it to medium. The phrase is verbatim: the row 'closes the part at web:Isa.59.21, its assigned range's final verse'. That names a writer-assignment boundary, not a literary one, and LF is right that Isaiah's text runs on into web:Isa.60.1. The point is stronger than LF states, and this is the REFINEMENT: web:Isa.59.21 | web:Isa.60.1 is NOT a frame seam under the eight-frame architecture — both verses sit inside the same parent frame — unlike the genuine frame boundary at web:Isa.55.13 | web:Isa.56.1. So once the batch wording is removed, this rear seam rests on a tier-3 single-witness seg alone, which can never drive, plus no stated tier-1 signal at all. That is a seam-warrant gap, not merely a register lapse. OL's items are UPHELD. (a) Frame forms: נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה closes oshb:Isa.59.20 — the postpositive signature — while oshb:Isa.59.21 carries אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה TWICE, a different frame census, after its fronted opening וַאֲנִ֗י זֹ֣את בְּרִיתִ֤י אוֹתָם֙ (all byte tier). The row's prose renders both formulas with the same English words and quotes neither, so a reader cannot see from the row which formula stands where — and the two seam judgements (not closing at web:Isa.59.20, holding web:Isa.59.21) each turn on one of them. (b) Chain overrun: the wayyiqtol chain byte-runs MT 59:15, MT 59:16 and MT 59:17, whose last link is תִּלְבֹּ֔שֶׁת (byte tier); MT 59:18's verbs are imperfect — כְּעַ֣ל יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם and גְּמ֥וּל יְשַׁלֵּֽם (byte tier) — so carrying the chain on through MT 59:18 is not byte-supported, and the row's own device_notes correctly calls the chain a byte-checkable claim, which makes the overrun self-inflicted. (c) Cross-seam catchwords: the light-and-rising root runs וּמִמִּזְרַח שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ at oshb:Isa.59.19 straight into זָרָֽח closing oshb:Isa.60.1 and on through MT 60:2-60:3 (byte tier) — four consecutive verses across the seam — undisclosed, which matters more here than usual precisely because the seam has no tier-1 warrant of its own. Verified true: the mark disclosure is byte-correct — the SAMEKH keyed at MT 59:21 marks the break after that verse, this row's close, and no other mark, paseq or ketiv/qere object falls inside MT 59:15-59:21.
rulings.remedy: Author work order. (a) boundary_rationale: delete the assigned-range wording and give the rear seam a stated warrant from Isaiah's own text, or record honestly that the seam rests on the tier-3 seg with no tier-1 signal and re-open confidence accordingly — this seam is NOT a frame boundary, so the non-negotiable frame-seam treatment available elsewhere does not apply here. TEST: no field names a part, batch, assigned range or row order, and the rear-seam sentence must name a tier and a signal class. (b) boundary_rationale: splice both frame forms — the postpositive signature at oshb:Isa.59.20 and the doubled speech frame at oshb:Isa.59.21 — and name each census, so the two seam judgements rest on distinguishable objects. TEST: the two sentences must remain distinguishable with every English rendering deleted. (c) boundary_rationale: end the chain claim at MT 59:17 and state that MT 59:18's verbs are imperfect. TEST (the check that killed the original): each link asserted for the chain must be a spliced wayyiqtol form; MT 59:18 must fail that test and be excluded. (d) device_notes: disclose the cross-seam catchwords — the light-and-rising root running from oshb:Isa.59.19 through oshb:Isa.60.1-60.3, and the redeemer and salvation nouns returning in the following chapter — and say what they do and do not argue at a seam that has no tier-1 warrant.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: a confidence of high on a span that is exactly one whole chapter violates the calibration discipline capping whole-chapter spans at medium_low, and the title-count digit is wrong against its own inventory. OL: the boundary is byte-sound, but four checkable defects sit in its evidence — the title count is the plene-only miss, the closing recognition-formula recurrence is byte-false and untier-labeled, a span-internal paseq at the very verse the row argues is undisclosed, and the ketiv/qere gloss covers only one of the two staged forms.
rulings.grounds: Both primaries are right, and they CONVERGE on the title digit — one defect, two sightings — while the rest are distinct. The cap violation is machine-checkable and confirmed: WEB ch 60 runs verses 1-22 and MT ch 60 runs 1-22 (identity numbering here, outside both offset zones), so the span is the chapter entire, and the row carries confidence HIGH where the campaign's chapter-fallback rule caps whole-chapter spans at medium_low. This is a known recurring class with five members book-wide, so the cure is a class sweep, not a single edit. LF's high stands and governs the row. Title digit UPHELD, with OL's diagnosis preferred because it names the cause: the plene title run לָךְ֙ עִ֣יר (oshb:Isa.60.14, byte tier) stands in exactly 24 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, and MT 49:7 is NOT among them because that verse carries the DEFECTIVE spelling שָׂרִ֖ים וְיִֽשְׁתַּחֲוּ֑וּ (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse) beside the distinct suffixed epithet — 24 plus 1 = 25 title verses (12 in chs 1-39, 13 in chs 40-66). The row's 'a 24-verse signature title' is precisely what a plene-only needle returns, and it is a digit-bearing claim attached to a named object, so it is machine-checkable and wrong. Both in-span sites the row names are genuine title verses: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Isa.60.9) and the MT 60:14 form, both byte tier. Recurrence UPHELD and SHARPER than stated: the row's own run וְיָדַ֗עַתְּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ reaches byte tier at oshb:Isa.60.16 and tier NONE at oshb:Isa.60.22, whose close is אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּעִתָּ֥הּ אֲחִישֶֽׁנָּה (byte tier) with no knowing-verb at all. The only shared material is the two-token self-declaration, and even that is not a byte pair — אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ at MT 60:16 against אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה at MT 60:22 differ at byte AND at accent-stripped tier, meeting only at SKELETON, where the pair stands in 22 verses book-wide (sweep: 22 verses). So the two ends are not the same object, the recurrence carries no tier label, and strongest_rejected_alternative is built on an echo the bytes do not support as stated. Paseq UPHELD: the inventory records a paseq seg at MT 60:9 — the very verse the row argues in prose and lists in its refs — undisclosed, while the row does engage the setumot at both edges (both byte-correct under break-after keying: the seg keyed at MT 59:21 marks the break after that verse, this row's front seam, and the seg keyed at MT 60:22 marks the break after its closing verse) and the ketiv/qere at MT 60:21.
